text: Augustine does not stop at posing the puzzle; his own positive answer — the first great phenomenological account of time in Western philosophy — is that time is a ___, a stretching or extension of the soul.
explanation: The book gives Augustine's proposed answer as the distentio animi, the 'distension of the mind,' on which past, present, and future are modes of attention — memory, attention, and anticipation. This is distinct from his more famous statement of the problem ('if no one asks me, I know...'); the blank asks specifically for his positive solution.
